name: Nimble Trunnion
description: Plant the feet wide beside the wheel so the body stays clear of recoil while the crew works the piece.

name: Judging Linstock
description: Thrust the wet sponge to the breech of the bore and twist twice to smother stray embers before loading.

name: Skipping Wheelhub
description: Carry the powder cartridge against the chest and walk it to the muzzle without letting a spark touch it.

name: Cascabel Note
description: Drive the rammer head down the bore in two firm strokes to seat cartridge and shot against the breech.

name: Cannonreview
description: Push the vent pick through the touch-hole to feel that the cartridge bag is pierced and the channel is open.

name: Recoildrop
description: Stand to the side, lower the lit portfire to the vent and step back as the gun roars and the shot leaves.

name: Measured Muzzleswell
description: Dip the sponge head, wring it half dry against the bucket rim and shoulder the staff ready for the bore.

name: Calm Touchhole
description: Screw the worm into the bore and draw it out to bring up scraps of old cartridge cloth.

name: Smooth Quoin
description: Pump the rammer one short stroke to press a loose wad flat against the shot.

name: Settled Carriage
description: Hold the long sponge staff across the chest to turn aside a shove from a crowding crewman or a stray blade.

name: Quoinbump
description: Swing the butt end of the sponge staff into a foe's ribs when raiders rush the muzzle.

name: Quoingauge
description: Set the iron-shod handspike under the trail and bear down with both hands to swing the gun a hand's breadth left.

name: Shifting Breechrope
description: Heave the trail end sideways with the bar braced on the thigh and walk the piece round.

name: Sideways Ballshot
description: Lean a shoulder to the wheel rim and push through two spokes to roll the gun forward on level ground.

name: Soft Linstock
description: Knock the wooden quoin under the breech with a mallet to raise or lower the muzzle by one notch.

name: Gunbore Stay
description: Swing the handspike up edge-on to turn aside a thrown stone or short blade aimed at the gun.

name: Sudden Recoil
description: Whip the handspike's iron toe around into the knee of a raider who slips between the wheels.

name: Resting Touchhole
description: Crouch behind the carriage cheek and set both feet so the body is not thrown when the gun rolls back.

name: Steady Breechrope
description: Fold and tie the flannel bag mouth so powder stays dry and the bag does not snag in the bore.

name: Quoinstay
description: Slap the tub lid shut and kneel over it to keep falling embers away from the loose powder.

name: Skipping Cannonade
description: Run bent low with the cartridge satchel on the hip from the magazine cart to the gun without jostling it.

name: Kind Gunbore
description: Heft a cartridge in the palm and judge by feel whether the charge is full, short or damp.

name: Tending Quoin
description: Press the flannel cartridge home against the breech with the rammer so no air gap lies behind the shot.

name: Warm Muzzleswell
description: Sweep spilled grains off the platform with a wet broom so no spark can ride them back to the tub.

name: Deep Trunnion
description: Stand in a line and hand cartridges forward at a steady count so the gunner is never kept waiting.

name: Resting Carriage
description: Throw a wet sack over a smoldering cartridge scrap and stamp it flat before it reaches the tub.

name: Shotreview
description: Close one eye and run the gaze along the ridge of the barrel to the mark to find the line of aim.

name: Judging Cascabel
description: Read the muzzle swell against the breech ridge to correct the aim for a short drop at the mark.

name: Gentle Gunbore
description: Hang a weighted cord from the trunnion to check that both wheels stand level before laying the gun.

name: Kind Breechrope
description: Count the notches on the elevation wedge and set the breech so the shot drops at the marked distance.

name: Straight Cannonade
description: Lay the muzzle level on a close mark and fire a flat round shot straight into it.

name: Kept Linstock
description: Drop behind the carriage cheek the instant the portfire touches so the blast passes overhead.

name: Quoinpace
description: Drop the trail ring over the limber hook in one motion and pin it before the team starts.

name: Tending Touchhole
description: Settle a breath of qi into the arms and lift the trail end onto the limber pintle without a second pair of hands.

name: Roarskitter
description: Walk beside the lead horse with the gun behind and shorten the stride on a slope.

name: Planted Carriage
description: Stamp the trail spade into soft ground with a heel so the carriage holds firm when it fires.

name: Broadside Pace
description: Shoulder the axle end and push the carriage out of a rut while the crew lifts the other wheel.

name: Cannonpause
description: Kick a chock under the wheel rim so the piece stays put on a slope while the crew loads.

name: Cascabel Gauge
description: Flip the limber box lid with the forearm and draw a cartridge in one hand while the other holds the lid.

name: Shotnote
description: Press a leather thumb stall over the touch-hole while the bore is sponged so no draught fans an ember.

name: Trunnion Gauge
description: Run the vent pick into the touch-hole with a quick twist to clear the channel of fouling.

name: Quoinnote
description: Slide the priming quill into the vent and let a thin trickle of fine powder run down it.

name: Light Roar
description: Step out sideways at the touch of the match and keep the match arm clear of the wheel.

name: Roardash
description: Hold a calm breath over a steadied qi-laced hand and touch the match to the vent for a clean discharge.

name: Quoinpause
description: Square the hips well to the side of the wheel so the rolling carriage passes without catching a leg.

name: Kind Quoin
description: Haul the brake rope on the trail to slow the carriage as it rolls back after firing.

name: Roar Hop
description: Grip two spokes and walk the gun back two paces to clear a pile of spent wadding.

name: Easing Ballshot
description: Push the cooled gun forward onto its firing mark on a two count called by the gunner.

name: Shothusk
description: Wedge a plank behind both wheels so the recoil spends itself against an earth bank.

name: Shifting Wheelhub
description: Slip clear of the rolling arc of the wheel by stepping aside on the heel as the carriage returns.

name: Shotpause
description: Drop the trail sprag into the dirt as the gun leaps so the carriage digs in and stops short.

name: Firm Recoil
description: Brace a shoulder at the cheek and breathe out as the match falls so recoil sends the gun straight back.

name: Watching Wheelhub
description: Count paces to a marked tree and set the elevation notch by the tally.

name: Tending Trunnion
description: Watch which way the match smoke leans to judge a crosswind before the gun is laid.

name: Gentle Muzzleswell
description: Watch where the first shot kicks up earth and note whether it fell short or long of the mark.

name: Calm Breechrope
description: Move the elevation wedge half a notch toward the splash so the second shot falls closer.

name: Steady Linstock
description: Study the slope of the ground between gun and mark to learn whether a shot will drop early.

name: Shotdash
description: Lay the muzzle on a marked stake and fire a round shot along the line the tally set.

name: Watching Quoin
description: Slip a gauge ring over each iron ball and set aside any that sticks or rattles loose.

name: Shotgauge
description: Ram a wad of hay down onto the cartridge so the ball does not roll when the muzzle dips.

name: Quoinreview
description: Twist a rope wad snug around the ball and seat it with a steady push of the rammer.

name: Deep Muzzleswell
description: Roll the ball along the bore floor with a palm to feel for a flaw before seating it.

name: Cannonnote
description: Ram twice with a held breath so the wad and ball sit tight against the charge.

name: Judging Carriage
description: Yank the muzzle plug free by its strap and step aside before sponging and loading begin.

name: Recoilblow
description: Lay the muzzle low over hard ground and fire so the round shot skips along the earth into a line of foes.
